claims.rationale: build.zig is an undeclared shared writer: multiple lanes edit it without declaring holds, silently invalidating suite measurements and creating latent work-loss bugs. The blast radius requires quantification before a mechanism can be chosen.

new_rows.claim: build.zig is an undeclared shared writer across infra lanes; editing without declaring holds silently invalidates suite measurements and creates latent work-loss bugs.

notes: T922 observation: T908 (glm-5.2) and T910 (deepseek-v4-pro) both had uncommitted edits to build.zig without declaring it in their holds. The one-writer hold rule (T500) never engaged because build.zig is the file that decides what zig build test runs, and nearly every regression row wires a new test_step dependOn as its last step. Two lanes editing one file with no serialization means one lane's wiring can vanish under the other's write, and the loss is silent — the row still closes pass, its script exists, and only the missing dependOn line says otherwise.
